mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level, indicative of accommodative monetary policy, compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 4.0%, or Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, or Rank IC over 5-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) over the past month indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer and business demand, which is a leading indicator of negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline in the prior month, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained macro regime (indicated by INDPRO growth below 0.5% annually), inflationary pressures and reduced corporate profitability lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO growth is below 0.5% annually, or Rank IC over 5-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.0% indicates accelerating inflation, which typically precedes monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) consistently signals robust consumer demand and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS growth is above 0.5% monthly, or Rank IC over 5-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (indicated by GDPC1 growth above 3.0% annually), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to valuation compression and policy tightening risks.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 3.0% annually, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a supply shock coupled with monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines and FEDFUNDS rises, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
